answer: A single sparrow chirp cannot fake a grove, because peers only count a signal when it is backed by bonded reputation and cross-validated by independent witnesses. A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is stake-weighted attestation with a per-epoch identity cost: each agent must lock a bond and pass a liveness challenge, so spinning up fake identities becomes expensive. Attackers must pay the full bond for every fake agent and risk slashing, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
